newsitem.title: UK: UK election delays MMC report on TransCo.
newsitem.headline: UK election delays MMC report on TransCo.

text.p: The publication of a Monopolies and Merger Commission report on controversial proposals for a new pricing regime for gas pipeline operator TransCo, part of BG Plc, will only take place after the elections on May 1.
The Department of Trade and Industry said that secretary of state Ian Lang will not take a look at report or any other MMC inquiry ahead of the election.
"This will be a matter for the new government," a DTI spokesman said.
The MMC aims to hand over its findings to gas industry regulator Ofgas on April 13. The watchdog will then immediately pass it on to BG and the DTI.
But the report can only be made public after the DTI's go-ahead.
The MMC has been vetting Ofgas's price proposals since October after they had been rejected by BG, which was then still called British Gas.

At the time, the company argued the proposals, which seek a 20 percent cut this year in TransCo's charges to gas suppliers, would leave it with insufficient funds to maintain an efficient and reliable pipeline network.
If accepted, the price proposals would also lead to a drastic cut in BG's dividend, investors fear.
